highlight.text: which method of working was the cartoon that our old masters used to make for painting in fresco, for greater rapidity; for having distributed the whole work over the plaster, they would outline it with the brush, reproducing from a small design all that which they wished to paint, and enlarging in proportion all that they thought to put down.

work.text: He was commissioned to paint a series of frescos for the porch of the Avignon Cathedral of which only the faint sinopia outlines remain.
In a triangular space above the lunette, the Saviour sits in benediction between six angels in graceful motion, airing their draperies in the wind.

moment.text: he was summoned with very great insistence to the Court of the Pope at Avignon, where he wrought so many pictures, in fresco and on panels, that he made his works correspond to the reputation that had been borne thither.

matters.text: This undoubtedly genuine production shows that Simone was at Avignon in his prime, free from the fetters of the old style as far it was possible for a Sienese painter to be, and graceful if not severe in the rendering of form.

source.author: J. A. Crowe and G. B. Cavalcaselle
source.title: A History of Painting in Italy, vol. 3: The Sienese School of the Fourteenth Century (ed. Langton Douglas)

matters.text: Simone Martini died while in the service of the Papal court at Avignon in 1344, having likely moved there in 1334 or 1335.
